indicators.flag: A	customer’s	photo	is	internally	inconsistent	(e.g.,	shows	visual	tells	of	being	altered)	or	is	inconsistent	with	their	other	identifying	information
indicators.red_flag: Photo alteration tells or photo–DOB age mismatch
indicators.rationale: Cross-checking a photo against DOB is partly doable from KYC fields, but judging whether a photo shows GenAI alteration tells needs external deepfake-detection capability the bank does not hold internally.

indicators.flag: A	customer	presents	multiple	identity	documents	that	are	inconsistent	with	each	other.
indicators.red_flag: Mismatched identity documents across presented IDs
indicators.rationale: The bank holds the submitted identity documents at onboarding, so cross-document consistency checks are already partly performed and can be tightened into a systematic comparison.

indicators.flag: A	customer	uses	a	third-party	webcam	plugin	during	a	live	verification	check
indicators.red_flag: Third-party webcam plugin or channel-switching mid-verification
indicators.rationale: Detecting a virtual webcam plugin or mid-session channel switching requires onboarding-session liveness telemetry from the identity-verification vendor, which is not captured in core bank systems.

indicators.flag: A	customer	declines	to	use	multifactor	authentication	to	verify	their	identity.

build_logic.logic: Flag an account that declines MFA enrollment or reverts to single-factor auth within the first 30 days, especially when paired with a high-risk action (large transfer, payee add, profile change).
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → fraud-ops account-access review gate

indicators.rationale: Authentication-enrollment events are captured in the bank's own auth logs, so an MFA opt-out signal is buildable today from data already held; it is not yet a monitored detection.

indicators.flag:
A	reverse-image	lookup	or	open-source	search	of	an	identity	photo	matches	an	image	in	an
online	gallery	of	GenAI-produced	faces.
indicators.red_flag: Identity photo matches an online GenAI-face gallery
indicators.rationale: Matching an identity photo to an online gallery of GenAI faces depends on an external reverse-image / synthetic-face corpus the bank does not hold and would have to source.

indicators.flag: A	customer’s	photo	or	video	is	flagged	by	commercial	or	open-source	deepfake	detection	software.
indicators.red_flag: Photo / video flagged by deepfake-detection software
indicators.rationale: Many banks already run a commercial deepfake-detection tool at onboarding; the gap is integrating its score into the monitoring pipeline rather than treating it as a standalone vendor check.

indicators.flag:
GenAI-detection	software	flags	the	potential	use	of	GenAI	text	in	a	customer’s	profile	or
responses to prompts.
indicators.red_flag: Detection-flagged GenAI text in profile / prompt responses
indicators.rationale: Detecting GenAI-authored text in profile or prompt responses requires a specialized text-detection capability and the prompt-response corpus, neither of which the bank holds today.

indicators.flag: A	customer’s	geographic	or	device	data	is	inconsistent	with	the	customer’s	identity	documents.
indicators.red_flag: Geo / device data mismatched to identity documents

build_logic.logic: Flag when session IP geolocation or device fingerprint region is persistently inconsistent with the stated residence and the issuing region of the identity document on file.
build_logic.source: session IP/device telemetry + KYC residence and identity-document fields
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → fraud-ops account-access review gate

indicators.rationale: Login IP/device telemetry and the customer's stated residence plus identity-document region are all held by the bank, so a geo/device-vs-identity mismatch signal is buildable from existing data.

indicators.flag:
A	newly	opened	account	or	an	account	with	little	prior	transaction	history	has	a	pattern	of
rapid	transactions;	high	payment	volumes	to	potentially	risky	payees,	such	as	gambling
websites	or	digital	asset	exchanges
indicators.red_flag: New / thin-history account → rapid flow to risky payees, chargebacks

build_logic.logic: Flag a newly opened account (or one with thin prior history) showing a burst of rapid transactions, disproportionate payment volume to higher-risk payees (gambling sites, digital-asset exchanges), or elevated chargeback / rejected-payment rates.
build_logic.source: core transaction ledger + account-opening date + payee classification + chargeback/return records
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → fraud-ops transaction review gate

indicators.rationale: Account age, transaction velocity, payee risk classification, and chargeback/return data all live in the core ledger, so this rapid-risky-flow pattern is buildable now and is the strongest transaction-pattern signal in the alert.
